newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Orient Overseas signs US$360 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Orient Overseas signs US$360 mln loan.

text.p: Orient Overseas (International) Ltd (OOIL) has signed a US$360 million financing arrangement to fund a number of container ships currently deployed by the group's container liner division, the company said Tuesday.
The agreement, which was signed with a group of banks, involves a US$360 million facility with a 12-year term covering six 4,960-TEU sized container ships delivered during the last two years.
The deal was oversubscribed, OOIL said.

The arranger group was headed by Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp and includes ABN Amro Bank, Banque Indosuez, Chase Manhattan Bank, Commerzbank, Deutsche Bank, Deutsche Schiffsbank, ING Bank and Swiss Ship Mortgage Bank.
OOIL is controlled by the family of Hong Kong's chief-executive designate Tung Chee-hwa.
Tung resigned from his position as chairman and chief executive of the company last October. His brother C.C. Tung has assumed those posts.
